debug_info.actual_negative_prompt: low resolution, severe blur, out of focus, overexposed, underexposed, heavy noise, grain, compression artifacts, smearing, chromatic aberration, excessive skin smoothing, plastic look, oversaturated, harsh contrast, HDR artifacts, loss of tonal range, obvious color cast, white balance error, distortion, content logic errors, pseudo-text gibberish, typographical errors, spelling mistakes, watermarks, overlays.
debug_info.ori_prompt: A single red apple with a brown stem and one green leaf, centered on a warm cream background. Soft-clay 3D picture-book illustration style: rounded plump shape, thick warm dark-brown outline (not black), soft directional studio lighting from the upper-left at 45 degrees creating one large soft highlight and gentle core shadow, subtle ambient occlusion shadow underneath, no gradients beyond soft light-to-shadow falloff, no text, no watermark, no additional objects, high-quality children's book illustration, clean vector-like shapes, 1:1 square composition, plenty of whitespace around the subject.
debug_info.actual_prompt:
A high-quality 3D rendered soft-clay picture-book illustration image, presenting a warm, clean, and gently whimsical atmosphere with the overall color palette anchored in a smooth warm cream white background — the precise tone of fresh parchment or unbleached linen, neither stark white nor yellowed, but a soft luminous off-white that radiates quiet warmth. The entire composition is a perfect 1:1 square format, the single red apple placed precisely at the geometric center of the frame, surrounded on all four sides by generous, breathing whitespace that allows the subject to exist in complete visual solitude, every corner of the background remaining pure and uninterrupted cream, no texture grain, no noise, no environmental elements whatsoever.

The apple itself is the sole protagonist of the image, rendered in a rounded, plump, almost geometrically simplified form that speaks directly to the vocabulary of premium children's book illustration — its silhouette is softly organic yet deliberately stylized, the body swelling outward in a gentle ovoid shape with slightly pinched waist curvature suggesting natural fruit anatomy without any anatomical realism, the proportions leaning toward the charmingly chubby and approachable rather than botanically accurate. The surface material is a matte soft-clay finish, the kind of tactile quality one associates with hand-rolled polymer clay or fondant modeling — completely non-specular, absorbing light rather than reflecting it sharply, the surface reading as velvety and slightly powdery under studio illumination, with zero mirror-like gloss anywhere on the skin. The base color of the apple is a rich, saturated warm red — not a flat digital red but a living, breathing hue sitting between cherry red and tomato red, carrying subtle warm undertones that harmonize perfectly with the cream background, the color feeling like it was mixed from natural pigments rather than generated digitally.

The lighting is the soul of this image: a single soft directional studio light source positioned at the upper-left at exactly 45 degrees elevation and 45 degrees horizontal angle, casting a large, diffused, feather-edged highlight zone across the upper-left quadrant of the apple's surface — this highlight is broad and gentle, occupying roughly one-third of the visible face, its edges dissolving gradually into the mid-tone red through an extremely soft falloff with absolutely no hard boundary, no gradient banding, no artificial transition lines, only a continuous whisper of tonal shift that reads as pure volumetric form. The core shadow falls naturally on the lower-right side of the apple, a deep warm-toned shadow that is still clearly readable as red rather than black or gray, maintaining chromatic integrity throughout the shadow region, the darkest point sitting at the lower-right edge where the apple meets the implied ground plane. There are no secondary lights, no rim lights, no colored fill lights — only this single warm key light creating a clean, honest, three-dimensional reading of the form. Beneath the apple, a subtle ambient occlusion contact shadow pools gently against the cream background, soft-edged and low in contrast, just enough to anchor the apple visually to the surface and prevent it from floating, the shadow fading to nothing within a short radius around the base.

The outline of the apple is drawn with a thick, confident, hand-crafted dark-brown stroke — not pure black, but a warm deep brownish-dark tone that carries the same warmth as the stem and leaf, giving the entire illustration a unified hand-made clay toy quality, the line weight consistent and deliberate, slightly thicker at corners and curves where a real clay sculptor's tool would naturally deposit more material, the line having a slight organic wobble that distinguishes it from mechanical vector precision while still reading as clean and intentional. This outline encircles the entire apple silhouette including the stem and leaf attachment points, unifying all elements into a single cohesive illustrated object.

The brown stem rises from the top-center of the apple, short and stubby, approximately one-eighth the height of the apple body, rendered in the same matte soft-clay material language as the fruit itself, its color a warm medium brown with slightly darker tones at the base where it meets the apple skin, the stem surface showing the same gentle highlight-to-shadow volume treatment as the main body, the tip of the stem slightly rounded and blunt rather than pointed, maintaining the overall softness of the design language. Attached to the stem is a single small green leaf, the leaf shape simple and slightly heart-shaped with a gently pointed tip, rendered in a muted sage-to-medium green that sits comfortably within the warm palette without introducing coolness, the leaf surface also matte and clay-textured, catching a faint highlight along its upper-left edge from the same studio light source, the leaf casting a tiny soft shadow onto the stem below it, the leaf outline sharing the same thick warm dark-brown stroke as the rest of the illustration.

The rendering style sits precisely at the intersection of 3D volumetric rendering and flat picture-book illustration — the apple has genuine three-dimensional form and believable light interaction, yet the shapes remain clean and graphic, the surfaces free of photographic noise or complex material complexity, the overall aesthetic reading as a lovingly crafted physical clay sculpture photographed under controlled studio conditions and then refined into a pristine illustration-ready render. Ray tracing is used for the ambient occlusion contact shadow and the soft light falloff, global illumination ensures the warm cream background subtly bounces warm fill light back onto the shadow side of the apple, roughness values on the apple surface are set high to achieve the matte clay quality, reflectivity is near zero, subsurface scattering is minimal and warm-toned to give the red flesh a very slight inner glow. Camera is positioned at a neutral eye-level angle with a slight downward tilt of approximately 10 degrees, focal length equivalent to 85mm, depth of field set to keep the entire apple in sharp focus with no bokeh blur, ensuring every detail of the clay texture, outline stroke, and highlight falloff is rendered with maximum clarity. 8K ultra-high resolution, clean vector-like shape precision combined with rich 3D material depth, premium children's book illustration quality, immaculate and timeless.
